_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.fossil: As of June 2026, WTI crude trades at approximately $84.38 per barrel, Brent crude at $86.99 per barrel, and US regular gasoline at $4.00 per gallon. Henry Hub natural gas is priced at $2.80 per MMBtu and has exhibited the greatest volatility among these fuels when indexed to 2019 (set at 100). Natural gas spiked sharply in 2022 before retreating, whereas crude oil and gasoline prices generally moved more in tandem. This higher volatility in natural gas reflects its sensitivity to supply disruptions and demand fluctuations relative to oil products.
notes.transition: The levelised cost of electricity (LCOE), which measures the average cost to produce one megawatt-hour (MWh) over the lifetime of a power plant, shows solar PV at $44/MWh and onshore wind at $33/MWh globally. These renewable sources now cost less than new coal or gas-fired generation, which stand at $110/MWh and $76/MWh respectively. The approximately 90% decline in solar PV costs since 2010—from around $460/MWh to $44/MWh—indicates substantial advancements in technology and economies of scale, enhancing solar's competitiveness as a mainstream energy source.
notes.currency: Approximately 20% of global oil trade is estimated to be settled outside the US dollar, a share that is gradually increasing. Despite this, the US dollar continues to dominate international oil transactions. This shift is partly driven by Russia’s strategic pivot toward Asian buyers and transactions settled in alternative currencies such as the yuan and rupee. It is important to note that the 20% figure is an estimate due to the lack of official comprehensive data.
notes.now: Today's energy landscape features moderately priced crude and gasoline with natural gas remaining the most volatile fuel, reflecting differing market dynamics. Concurrently, renewable energy sources like solar and onshore wind have become economically more attractive than new fossil fuel-based power generation, driven by significant cost reductions. Meanwhile, the international currency composition of oil trade is slowly diversifying, although the US dollar remains predominant.
